Subject: Deployment mode & EU data residency - quick follow-up

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the call this morning - that was helpful. Two quick clarifications we need before we loop in procurement and legal: 1) For production traffic, can Redwood ensure all EU customer data (requests + logs) stay in an EU region if we use Hosted API? 2) If we go Dedicated or Private VPC, how different is the timeline and what dependencies do you need from our infra team?

High level: Nordbank prefers hosted-first if we can guarantee EU-only residency for both model invocation and logs. If Hosted won't meet that, procurement is likely to push for Dedicated or Private.

Can you confirm and share any SOC2 / dataflow artifacts we can give to our security team?

Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU data residency - quick follow-up

Thanks Simon - great questions. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Hosted API: We can serve and store request/response data within an EU region for production if you require EU-only residency, but there are caveats around logs/analytics retention and third-party routing for infra management (we offer EU-only routing and can disable cross-region fallbacks for strict residency).
- Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPU pools in EU give you stronger guarantees and isolation; logs and metrics remain in your region by default.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full control - customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integrations, and no cross-region routing. Longer lead time (typically 6-10 weeks) depending on your infra approvals and network setup.

Attachments: SOC2 summary and a simple EU dataflow diagram attached for your security team to review.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I'll loop Marissa (deployments/solutions) and Rishi (security/compliance) to confirm the specific Hosted SLOs and any routing options we can disable.
2) If procurement is leaning Private/Dedicated, can you share a preferred timeline and a contact on your infra team for a technical kickoff?

I'm available for a 30-minute technical follow-up tomorrow or Friday. What works for you?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Simon Janssen <simon.janssen@nordbank.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T14:45:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU data residency - quick follow-up

Hi Simon - following up with technical details on the Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for EU residency: 

Hosted API (EU-only mode):
- We can pin all inference requests and logs to an EU region (we currently support eu-west-1 and eu-central-1).
- Cross-region fallback is configurable; for strict residency we can disable automatic fallback to non-EU model cache nodes.
- Note: some operational metadata (short-lived control-plane traces) may still transit for telemetry; we can provide a telemetry contract and retention policy for review.

Dedicated:
- Dedicated GPU pools in EU with tenant isolation; logs and metrics are written only to your customer-specific EU storage.
- Faster support SLA and optional on-prem connectors for secure upload of encryption keys.

Private VPC / On-prem:
- Full networking control, recommended for regulated PII workflows. Lead time driven by your network and security review; typical delivery 6-10 weeks after kickoff.

Action items for your team:
- If Hosted is acceptable, confirm whether you need eu-west-1 vs eu-central-1 (we can provision EU-only tenancy in either).
- If you need Dedicated/Private, share preferred kickoff dates and an infra contact for IP allowlisting and KMS integration.

I've attached a short EU dataflow diagram and a draft SOW that outlines timelines per deployment mode. Happy to join a technical call to run through any questions.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
